title: Medical QA: published GPT-3.5 aggregate accuracies
analysis_unit: Question within each benchmark, not patient or training run
aggregation: Proportion correct for each task; no pooling across datasets
error_definition: No bars plotted; source reports plus/minus as standard deviation of proportion, not CI or across-seed SD; retained in raw CSV only
scope: Real public aggregate table replot; original models and experiments were not rerun
caption: Replot of real published aggregate accuracies from Xiong et al., Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, ACL Findings 2024, DOI10.18653/v1/2024.findings-acl.372, Table6 GPT-3.5-16k-0613 rows. CoT is the no-retrieval baseline; MedRAG uses MedCorp, RRF-4 and 32 retrieved snippets. Each row is a different question benchmark, with question denominators from Table2 shown in labels. Values are percent correctly answered; a common 0–100 range is used (padding for markers and labels). No uncertainty bars or significance tests are added. The source plus/minus column is retained in the raw CSV, not reinterpreted as a confidence interval. PubMedQA* follows the paper's modified setting. No patient-level outcome, pooled accuracy or original experiment reproduction is claimed. Original table transcription was visually checked; this artifact validates real aggregate-data adaptation and reproducible rendering.
